manchete.resumo: In this episode of the No Film School Podcast , independent film producer Stephen Mastrocola joins host GG Hawkins to discuss the current state of indie film financing, production, and distribution, including his…
manchete.trecho: In this episode of the No Film School Podcast , independent film producer Stephen Mastrocola joins host GG Hawkins to discuss the current state of indie film financing, production, and distribution, including his takeaways from the 2026 American Film Market (AFM). As the co-founder of Static Films and a former executive producer at Buffalo 8, Stephen shares how he went from working on low-budget productions to developing financing strategies for emerging filmmakers. They break down the decline of traditional pre-sales and minimum guarantees, the role of tax incentives and debt financing, and why building an audience acquisition strategy before production may be more valuable than securing a distributor. Stephen also discusses lessons from producing films like Wine Club , Crossword , and Mazel Tough , the importance of long-term creative relationships, and how independent filmmakers can…

noticias.trecho: fabrizio giugiaro introduces his copper-bodied peralta D   Italian automotive designer Fabrizio Giugiaro and his studio GFG Style unveil the Peralta D, a one-off supercar with bodywork made entirely from hand-hammered copper . Presented at the Pastejé Automotive Invitational in Mexico in October 2026, the Maserati-based grand tourer revisits the angular automotive design language that the designer’s father, Giorgetto Giugiaro, helped establish in the 1960s and 1970s.   The car has the appearance of a solid piece of polished metal, even across its expansive windshield and roof. A specially treated mirrored glass canopy takes on the reddish tones of the copper below, and the distinction between the two materials nearly disappears when the car is viewed in profile.   The project follows GFG Style’s 2025 Peralta S, a sports car sculpted from mirror-polished aluminum and inspired by…

noticias.titulo: Why Camille Walala is transforming a metro station with 30,000 hand-made tiles inspired by basketball
noticias.resumo: Alley-Oop, the French-born artist’s first permanent public artwork, pays tribute to a basketball legend and an architectural landmark. If you’ve spent any time in East London, you’ll probably have come across Camille…
noticias.trecho: Alley-Oop, the French-born artist’s first permanent public artwork, pays tribute to a basketball legend and an architectural landmark. If you’ve spent any time in East London, you’ll probably have come across Camille Walala’s work, albeit perhaps unknowingly; from the Dream Come True Building on Old Street to the stretch of Leyton High Street she covered in grids, triangles and stripes. Now the French-born, London-based artist is bringing her colourful, Memphis-influenced style to the platforms of Flachet–Alain Gilles metro station in Villeurbanne, part of greater Lyon, France, which serves around 5.7 million passengers a year. Set for completion next Spring, the installation, titled Alley-Oop, has been created from more than 30,000 hand-crafted ceramic tiles. This will be the biggest project of Camille’s career to date. It’s also her first permanent public-realm work, her first major…

Run with the Semi-Wild Yilki Horses of Anatolia in Nur Tucker’s Captivating Photos
referencias.resumo: Around the dusty plains and otherworldly volcanic rock formations of the historical region of Cappadocia , a millennia-old tradition continues. Here in Central Anatolia, Turkey, horses have been a part of daily life…
referencias.trecho: Around the dusty plains and otherworldly volcanic rock formations of the historical region of Cappadocia , a millennia-old tradition continues. Here in Central Anatolia, Turkey, horses have been a part of daily life, civic programs, and military campaigns since prehistory. In The Untold Story of the Yilki Horse , photographer Nur Tucker captures a portrait of the region’s living heritage. Published by Hemeria, the title delves into the beauty and tenacity of the semi-wild horses while also highlighting the lifestyles of those who herd them through rugged landscapes. Tucker, who is a British-Turkish photographer based in the U.K., has long been drawn to the vigor and elegance of horses, and the yilki breed that populates Anatolia have a particularly resonant history. “Yilki” comes from the Turkish verb yılmak , which means “to flee” or “to be set loose.” The name “has come to describe…

biblioteca.resumo: O livro de Manuel Rivas, El lápiz del carpintero, publicado em 1998, é ambientado na Galícia durante a Guerra Civil espanhola. Há, porém, uma ligação com o presente, liderada pelo objeto/personagem do título. É por meio…
biblioteca.trecho: O livro de Manuel Rivas, El lápiz del carpintero, publicado em 1998, é ambientado na Galícia durante a Guerra Civil espanhola. Há, porém, uma ligação com o presente, liderada pelo objeto/personagem do título. É por meio desse fio condutor, também, que a narrativa une história real e ficção. A partir da análise do livro, este artigo pretende investigar como esse traço narrativo é traduzido intersemióticamente no filme homônimo do diretor Antón Reixa, de 2003, e também visa compreender a percepção de como nos dois títulos (livro e filme) se aglutinam as experiências referentes à memória e à identidade.

bolhas.titulo: Up Close: Amar Kanwar’s “The Charcoal Man”
bolhas.resumo: Amar Kanwar Serpentine North Gallery London Sep 23, 2026–Jan 31, 2027 As I fall asleep, I get glimpses into strangers’ lives—disjointed scenes and non-sequiturs embellished with flashes of vivid emotion, some mine, some…
bolhas.trecho: Amar Kanwar Serpentine North Gallery London Sep 23, 2026–Jan 31, 2027 As I fall asleep, I get glimpses into strangers’ lives—disjointed scenes and non-sequiturs embellished with flashes of vivid emotion, some mine, some not. You could call them hypnagogic hallucinations. Watching Amar Kanwar’s The Charcoal Man (2026) feels like that. The video installation looks back on the attempts on Gandhi’s life before and after the 1947 Partition of India, but its 12 magical-realist stories, each centering a distinct character, seep beyond this timeline. The work distills the era’s violence, division, and forced migration into the prosaic experiences and actions of individuals, whose tales—told through text alongside found and shot footage across seven channels—abound in ambiguities and unresolved quandaries, as in dreams and waking life. Presenting fragments without their resolution is a…

bolhas.trecho: Daniel Herrera Carbajal ICT Mary Peltola has named Raina Thiele as her chief of staff as she prepares to be sworn in as Alaska’s first Native American senator. Thiele, Dena’ina Athabascan and Yup’ik, served as a senior political advisor on Peltola’s Senate campaign following four years as the senior advisor for Alaska affairs and strategic priorities at the Department of the Interior when Deb Haaland, Laguna Pueblo, served as Interior secretary during the Biden administration. Thiele also served for seven years in the executive office under President Barack Obama where she served in the Office of Management and Budget before becoming associate director of the Office of Intergovernmental Affairs and Public Engagement. Among the majority of participants who maintain a presence in the Asia Pacific region, 27 are from Hong Kong, including Alisan Fine Arts, Blindspot Gallery, Empty Gallery, gdm, Kiang Malingue, and Rossi & Rossi. bolhas.trecho: Kevin Abourezk ICT MIDDLETOWN, Iowa – Indigenous voices are rising against a U.S. Army plan to detonate bomb-making chemicals that could release a toxic plume downwind of the explosion site.  The plan for the controlled detonation of 68 barrels of degraded lead azide at an Army facility in Middletown, Iowa, has drawn health and environmental concerns – and lawsuits – is now scheduled on Wednesday after a three-judge panel of the 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals approved the plan Monday, saying there were adequate safeguards to minimize dust dispersal.  The idea is not being welcomed in Indigenous communities. “As stewards of the land, our responsibility to protect the earth, water, and all living things extends beyond our own borders, and we stand in deep concern for our neighbors and the lands in the path of this blast,” the Iowa-based Meskwaki Nation Tribal Council said in a…
